solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In dome, unveils new statue

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the two words are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Inside a dome, someone unveils a freshly made statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link word; DOME and UNVEILS together give the eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo is a famous ancient Greek marble statue in the Louvre.

clue.text: French writer displaying anger after dance

indicators.note: after places the word for anger behind the word for the dance

parts.note: the volta is a lively Renaissance dance
ire means anger

explanation.surface: A French author loses their temper after a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire was the pen name of the French Enlightenment author François-Marie Arouet.

clue.text: Denying, say, being caught in local

indicators.note: being caught in places the abbreviation for say inside the word for local

parts.note: a local is a native of the place
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Someone denies, for instance, being caught in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like a British pub but here means a native resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative reply is a denying one, an adjective for refusing or contradicting.

clue.text: Greek god — son joining a Norse god

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
Tyr is the Norse god of war

explanation.surface: A Greek deity's son marries into the family of a Norse god.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs are woodland deities of Greek myth, part man and part goat.

clue.text: Stone me! Messenger's topless outside

indicators.note: outside means the shortened messenger word wraps around the word me
topless removes the first letter of the word for messenger

parts.note: a herald is a messenger
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a messenger appearing topless outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me!' reads as a British exclamation of surprise, but 'Stone' alone is the definition. 'topless' turns HERALD into ERALD, which goes 'outside' ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a precious green gemstone.

clue.text: Under control at home, central European, reportedly

parts.note: being at home is being in

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is spoken, so the nationality sounds like a different spelling

parts.note: a Czech comes from central Europe

explanation.surface: A central European at home keeps things under control, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something restrained or contained is the idiom for having it under control.

clue.text: Primate telephoned, absorbed by published article

indicators.note: absorbed by places the word for telephoned inside the word for published

parts.note: a book that is out is published
rang means telephoned
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A primate is described as having phoned and featured in a published article.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, one of the primates.

clue.text: There's nothing in prison I like

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the run of words prison I like

explanation.surface: A prisoner remarks that there is nothing in jail they enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is zero, a synonym for nothing, as in sports scores.

clue.text: Idea unacceptable about island

indicators.note: about means the phrase for unacceptable goes round the island letter

parts.note: something that is not on is unacceptable
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a plan concerning an island as out of the question.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT ON is British slang for unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a thought or concept, a close synonym for idea.

clue.text: Large snake makes one run

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an adder is a snake

explanation.surface: A big snake gives someone a fright that makes them flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a run in stockings or tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder is a vertical line of unravelled stitches in tights, also called a run.

clue.text: Run away on one heading for Tokyo

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone flees, setting off for Tokyo.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG IT is informal for running away; the cricket sense of 'on' as the leg side is the crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To leg it is a slang idiom meaning to flee on foot.

clue.text: Break dance, then, delighted

indicators.note: break means the letters of the two words are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A breakdancing routine, after which the audience were thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchanted describes being charmed or filled with pleasure, synonym of delighted.

clue.text: Substitute to change number towards end of tie

parts.note: to alter is to change
at means towards, as in aiming at

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the word tie

explanation.surface: A football replacement is brought on to shift the score late in a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' suggests a drawn game, but only its final letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternate is a stand-in or reserve who takes another's place.

clue.text: Item of wear girl's beginning to be very fond of

indicators.note: beginning takes the first letter of the word girl's

parts.note: to love is to be very fond of

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing a girl is starting to adore.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove is a garment worn on the hand, so an item of clothing.

clue.text: With no end of exertion, man of the cloth worshipped

indicators.note: with no means the following letter is taken out of the clergyman word

parts.note: a reverend is a clergyman

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of exertion

explanation.surface: Without any effort, a priest was venerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Revered means deeply respected or venerated, a synonym for worshipped.

clue.text: Lose vigour — manage to consult foremost of doctors

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
taken as written
to see a specialist is to consult one

indicators.note: foremost of takes the first letter of doctors

explanation.surface: Someone feeling run down arranges to see the leading doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: Plants that run to seed stop producing and decline, hence losing vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes deteriorating or becoming shabby, so losing strength.

clue.text: Equipment placed next to English aircraft

parts.note: kit means equipment

explanation.surface: Gear is set alongside an English plane.
explanation.walkthrough: KITE is old RAF slang for an aeroplane, and a kite is itself a flying craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a tethered flying craft, and in slang an aeroplane.

clue.text: Unmarried man, composer, character upset

parts.note: J S Bach is the German composer

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for character upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a role is a character in a play

explanation.surface: A single man, a composer, is an upset character.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is a man who has never married.

clue.text: Hold on to Japanese drink as a memento

parts.note: to keep something is to retain it
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a bottle of Japanese rice wine as a souvenir.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small item kept in memory of someone, a memento.

clue.text: Burden borne by America?

parts.note: something borne by a person is carried on them
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A load that the United States must carry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'borne by America' as 'on the US'; a burden that is on us.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus means a responsibility or duty, a burden one must bear.

clue.text: Check opening for caretaker

parts.note: to check something is to stop it
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: Examining a hole for the building's janitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caretaker' looks like a janitor but is the adjective, as in a caretaker government.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary substitute, just as a caretaker leader holds office for now.

clue.text: A charge — chap gets time

parts.note: a chap is a man
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: A man is given a date for his case after being charged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an authority or commission entrusted to someone, a charge.

clue.text: Head of state needs month to carry on

indicators.note: to carry means the month word holds the word on inside it

parts.note: March is a month
taken as written

explanation.surface: A president needs a month to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry on' looks like one phrase, but 'carry' is the container and 'on' its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a king or queen, the sovereign head of a state.

clue.text: Hand hand fruit

parts.note: a paw is a hand, informally
a paw is a hand again

explanation.surface: Fruit is passed from hand to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawpaw is another name for papaya, a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Dog wager — fool collected!

indicators.note: collected means the wager word gathers up the word for fool inside it

parts.note: a bet is a wager
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A dog bet, and the idiot gathered his winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged hound breed.

clue.text: Area hit hard round historical Franciscan mission

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit hard
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A region battered around an old Franciscan mission.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in Texas began as a Franciscan mission before its famous 1836 siege.

clue.text: Title of different wine shop is about right

indicators.note: is about means the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for right
different signals that the letters of wine shop are rearranged

explanation.surface: The ownership of a different wine shop concerns rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Title in law means the right to own property, so legal possession.

clue.text: Come to a stretch of open water

definitions.meaning: a straight length of a river or a stretch of sea

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at a stretch of open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Reach means arrive at, and also a continuous stretch of river between bends.

clue.text: Commuter's ticket — green, possibly

parts.note: a pass is a ticket for travel or entry

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of green may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A commuter's travel pass is perhaps green in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter is someone carried on a train or bus, a traveller who is not the driver.

clue.text: Each and every adult touring old Scottish town

indicators.note: touring means the first pieces travel round the abbreviation for old

parts.note: all means each and every
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: All the adults go touring an ancient town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLOA is a small town in Clackmannanshire, central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town on the River Forth in central Scotland.

clue.text: Hold back discarding a joker

indicators.note: discarding means the letter a is thrown out of the word for hold back

parts.note: to wait is to hold back

explanation.surface: A card player holds back, throwing away a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joker' suggests a playing card but means a witty person.
explanation.definitionFit: A wit is a clever, funny person who makes jokes.

clue.text: Department's demand involving hydrogen bomb

indicators.note: involving means the department and demand pieces take the hydrogen symbol into them

parts.note: dept is the abbreviation for department
a charge is a demand for payment
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A government department demands payment over the hydrogen bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A depth charge is an anti-submarine explosive set to detonate underwater.
